texts.facts: In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act and same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. Further, a private petition u/s 166 MV Act was also filed. As such both were merged together. 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 16.03.2015 at MACT No. 2225/15 Ramesh Chander v. Hitesh Page No. 2 of 24 BK about 12.30 pm, injured/ original petitioner Ramesh Chander was going on foot alongwith other co-employees. When he reached at Nizamuddin Khatta before red light, National Highway-24 in proper manner, all of a sudden one Maruti Echo vehicle bearing no. DL-1RT-3355 came at high speed and in rash and negligent manner and hit the injured/original petitioner forcefully due to which he fell down on the road and sustained multiple grievous injuries. He was removed to AIIMS Trauma Center for his treatment. Further, he also received permanent disability. 3. Further, Medical Board of AIIMS, New Delhi sent disability report noticing 90% permanent physical disability in relation to both upper limbs and right lower limb. 4. An FIR bearing No. 163/15, u/s 279,338 IPC PS Sunlight Colony, New Delhi was registered in this case. 5. In response to DAR and petition, initially respondent no.1/driver Hitesh, respondent No.2/owner Harish Chawla as well as insurance company/respondent no.3 appeared and filed their replies. 6. A stand is taken by insurance company that claim raised by the injured is on higher side. It is further stated that he failed to prove the loss of income. It is further stated that he is a government employee working in DTC as driver, therefore, there was no loss of income. But it appears that no statutory defence raised by the insurance company in present case. 7. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed on 26.07.2018 by Predecessor of this Tribunal: 1. Whether injured Ramesh Chander suffered MACT No. 2225/15 Ramesh Chander v. Hitesh Page No. 3 of 24 BK injuries in a road traffic accident on 16.03.2015 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. DL-1RT-3355 being driven by R-1,owned by R-1 and insured with R-3? In this case, as per record, during pendency of this petition which is one of the oldest twenty matters, original petitioner Ramesh Chander expired due to reasons unconnected with original injury. Therefore, an application impleading his legal heirs was filed and same was allowed by my learned Predecessor vide order dated 01.11.2021. 9. In this case, five witnesses are examined on behalf of petitioner including petitioner himself. 10. PW-1 Ashok Kumar brought the pay certificate of the injured and same is Ex. PW-1/1. Again another PW-1 Mahipal Singh brought the leave record, appointment letter and salary status of the original injured. He further stated during his cross-examination, cost of medicine were reimbursed to the injured from DTC. PW-3 is the original injured himself. He proved his overall case and was cross-examined by learned counsel for insurance company. PW-4 is another witness from DTC who brought leave record Ex. PW-4/D and service record Ex. PW-4/E and attendance register Ex. PW-4/C. PW-5 is another witness who proved entire leave record of deceased as Ex. PW-5/1 and copy of pay fixation detail showing loss of salary, Ex. PW-5/2. MACT No. 2225/15 Ramesh Chander v. Hitesh Page No. 4 of 24 BK 11. Further, from perusal of record, it can be seen although R-1 and R-2 filed their joint reply but they did not participate in proceeding later on. Further, they did not leave any evidence in support of their stand taken in their original reply. Further, as per record, R-3/insurance company did not lead any evidence in its support. 15. In the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. The IO has filed Detailed Accident Report MACT No. 2225/15 Ramesh Chander v. Hitesh Page No. 5 of 24 BK before this Tribunal. 17. In present case, injured/ eye witness to the accident, PW-1 has deposed about the manner of accident and further deposed that accident occurred due to negligence of driver of offending vehicle.

In Bimla Devi & Ors vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ors [(2009) 13 SC 530,[ in Kaushnumma Begum and others v/s New India Assurance Company Limited, [2001 ACJ 421 SC[, in East Delhi vs Hitesh S/O Sh. Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana cited as [2009 ACJ 287], it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view is to be taken. It has been further held that the proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to the proceedings in a Civil Suit and hence, strict rules of evidence are not applicable. In National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 16. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess MACT No. 2225/15 Ramesh Chander v. Hitesh Page No. 7 of 24 BK the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. 23. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). MACT No. 2225/15 Ramesh Chander v. Hitesh Page No. 8 of 24 BK (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). 23.1. In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii) (a) and (iv). 23.2. It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the East Delhi vs Hitesh S/O Sh. Roshan Lal on 11 November, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14079428/ 5 heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. 23.3. Assessment of pecuniary damages under Item (i) and under Item (ii) (a) do not pose much difficulty as they involve reimbursement of actuals and are easily ascertainable from the evidence. 23.4. Award under the head of future medical expenses--Item (iii)--depends upon specific medical evidence regarding need for further treatment and cost thereof. 23.5. Assessment of non-pecuniary damages--Items (iv), (v) and (vi)--involves determination of l u m p s u m a m o u n t s w i t h r e f e r e n c e t o c i r c u m s t a n c e s s u c h a s a g e , n a t u r e o f injury/deprivation/disability suffered by the claimant and the effect thereof on the future life of the claimant. 23.6. It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the MACT No. 2225/15 Ramesh Chander v. Hitesh Page No. 9 of 24 BK assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). 23.7. MACT No. 2225/15 Ramesh Chander v. Thus, sufficient discretion has been given to the Tribunal not to insist on investment of the compensation amount in long term fixed deposit and to release even the whole amount in the case of literate persons.
